name: Analytics
description: First-party traffic analytics (port of q9's analytics app): an append-mode page_views collection fed by a server-side capture hook (object_analytics), one row per non-asset request -- path/method/status/ip/user_agent/referrer/session/is_owner. Live traffic + bot-attack visibility (4xx and /api hits ARE captured on purpose), and a rollup source for dashboards. Capture is off unless DBBASIC_ANALYTICS is set (per-request write is an operator choice); admin-read only, closed to the generic write surface. Bounded by the daemon's time-windowed retention pass (DBBASIC_ANALYTICS_RETENTION_DAYS, default 30) -- the platform's heaviest write path and the stress test for massive-file rotation. No pages: the shell/dashboard + rollups are the surface. 0.2.0 adds /visitors, which answers a different question from /analytics: not what was requested, but how many PEOPLE came. It counts visitors, bots and the operator's own traffic APART rather than as one number, because undifferentiated unique-IP counts are dominated by scanners -- on this very server 45% of distinct paths were hit exactly once by things probing for /wp-login.php -- and a metric that turns a quiet day into a busy one is worse than no metric. A bot is decided behaviourally (an address that never successfully loaded a real page) rather than by a user-agent blocklist, because the blocklist is always out of date and the behaviour is not. Our own hits are labelled, never hidden: seeing your own visit is how you know the page is recording anything at all.
